prompt: How do we determine our SWIFT architecture type, and why does it matter?
assertions: Explains the architecture taxonomy: A1 (full stack on premises), A2 (partial), A3 (connector), A4 (customer connector to external messaging), B (no local footprint — fully outsourced/browser access)
States why it matters: architecture type drives which CSCF controls apply (mandatory/advisory/N-A per type)
Notes the v2026 wrinkle: client connectors are mandatorily assessed under ~14 controls and some B users reclassify as A4
Walks a determination method: inventory SWIFT-related components (messaging interface, communication interface, connectors, GUI) and where they run
Connects to attestation: the type selected in KYC-SA determines the control set attested against — misclassification is an assessment finding
